War of October 1973 in which Egypt and Syria attacked Israel by surprise on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish year, to win back land lost in the Six-Day War of 1967.

Egypt under Anwar Sadat crossed the Suez Canal and Syria struck on the Golan Heights on 6 October. Israel's leaders, including Prime Minister Golda Meir, had trusted an idea called "the Concept": that Egypt would not attack without long-range air power. They ignored warnings, including one from King Hussein of Jordan, and did not strike first, partly fearing to lose US support.

The first days went badly for Israel. Then it held the north, crossed the canal, and trapped Egypt's Third Army. The United States airlifted arms to Israel, the Soviet Union backed the Arab side, and Arab oil states cut supply in the 1973 oil crisis. A UN ceasefire took hold on 25 October.

The war broke the idea that Israel was unbeatable. It led to the Camp David Accords and peace between Egypt and Israel in 1979.
sum: War of October 1973 in which Egypt and Syria attacked Israel by surprise on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish year, to win back land lost in the Six-Day War of 1967.
